title: Four covers, the first 3-page edition, and the factory's five beats
headline: Your positioning is on paper. The storyteller turned it into the factory's life in five beats, the same at every length from 1 to 150 pages, and wrote the 3-page edition told by the cast (a draft, attached). The designer drew four cover studies on it (attached). Three readers like the ones you named read the 3 pages: two would start tomorrow; the one closest to your Web Summit team wants to see several people, each with their own agents.

for_you.ask: Which cover? (one, or two to combine)
for_you.detail: A, the factory: the nine in a ring round one creator, the talk a small screen leaving the ring. B, the festival set-up: the stage small at the back, the team building in front. C, the map: the nine along genesis to commodity. D, the zoom: a frame per edition closing in. All under GEN ZX FOUNDERS, the title a placeholder until NS1.
Assembled, running, stopped; a non-talk example (a shop); step one with a how.

sections.title: The factory's life in five beats (the storyteller)
items: 1. The creator's problem: an idea, and a medium that fell short (inventing on principle)
2. The factory is assembled, in hours, from earlier pieces (Wardley's commoditisation)
3. The factory runs: build, check, show the creator, change, again; the talk gets made
4. The factory is stopped and taken apart: the hold, what never closed, what was kept
5. The factory is rebuilt: this book's own team; the Web Summit team next; the reader's own (Kelly)

sections.title: Worth knowing for the title and cover
sections.text: The researcher: in industry, 'agent factory' mostly names a vendor's platform (Microsoft's and Google's, from August 2025). Your sense, a team assembled for one objective and taken apart, is your own, so the book has to show it rather than lean on the phrase.
